research_note: These works collectively establish that your idea is technically credible. They also suggest that the novelty probably won't lie in introducing a gateway or adding policy checks. It will need to lie in how the gateway coordinates corrective interventions throughout execution.

resources.title: SAMOS — Securing MCP-based Agent Workflows
resources.description: SAMOS enforces information-flow policies at the MCP gateway, tracks session-level context, and blocks tool interactions that violate security constraints. A particularly close match to your gateway-level control concept.
resources.focus: Cross-tool information flow and session-aware enforcement.
resources.attribution: Grigoris Ntousakis, Julian James Stephen, Michael V. Le, Sai Sree Laya Chukkapalli, Teryl Taylor, Ian M. Molloy, and Frederico Araujo. © 2025 the authors. PACMI ’25, DOI: 10.1145/3766882.3767177.

resources.title: Governance by Construction for Generalist Agents
resources.description: IBM's CUGA governance approach intervenes at five checkpoints: intent, planning guidance, tool calls, approval and output. Unlike a gateway that simply rejects unsafe operations, it also steers agents towards compliant behaviour.
resources.focus: Runtime intervention across the agent lifecycle.
resources.attribution: Segev Shlomov, Iftach Shoham, Alon Oved, Ido Levy, Sami Marreed, Harold Ship, Offer Akrabi, Sergey Zeltyn, Avi Yaeli, and Nir Mashkif. © 2026 the authors. arXiv:2605.20874v1; related ACM DOI: 10.1145/3786335.3813192.

resources.title: AgentTrust — Runtime Safety Evaluation and Interception
resources.description: Intercepts actions before execution, detects risky multistep sequences, and can suggest safer alternatives through its SafeFix mechanism.
resources.focus: Correcting dangerous tool calls, not merely blocking them.
resources.availability: The supplied notes are reproduced below. The linked arXiv version uses arXiv's non-exclusive distribution licence, which does not grant this repository permission to redistribute the complete paper. Use the original HTML for the full text.

resources.title: Runtime Policy Enforcement for MCP-Based LLM Agents
resources.description: Implements deterministic enforcement at the tool-call boundary with cross-step sensitivity labels and tamper-evident audit records. The reported attack success rate fell from 40% to 5% in a controlled evaluation.
resources.focus: Deterministic enforcement independent of agent reasoning.
resources.availability: The supplied notes are reproduced below. The publisher blocked automated full-text retrieval during preparation, so no complete article is included locally. Read the original for the evaluation setup and limitations.

resources.title: The Task Shield — Enforcing Task Alignment
resources.description: Tests whether instructions and tool calls genuinely contribute to the user's original objectives. This is particularly relevant to stopping an agent from drifting away from an authorized task.
resources.focus: Aligning execution with original user intent.
resources.attribution: Feiran Jia, Tong Wu, Xin Qin, and Anna Squicciarini. © 2025 Association for Computational Linguistics. Proceedings of ACL 2025, pages 29680–29697. DOI: 10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.1435.

resources.title: ZT-MCP — A Zero-Trust Security Architecture
resources.description: Combines tool identity verification, capability-based authorization, output filtering and audit logging. This is the most directly named Zero Trust MCP architecture I found.

resources.title: Runtime Governance for AI Agents: Policies on Paths
resources.description: Formalizes runtime governance as a policy function over agent identity, the partial execution path, a proposed next action and organizational state. Explains why path-dependent rules require runtime checks, and discusses deployment designs and a reference implementation.
resources.focus: Path-dependent policies and per-action intervention across an execution history.
